title: Let a closed console session stop hearing config changes

blocks.text: The admin console opens a `ConfigSession` for every signed-in user, and each open session is told about every configuration change so its screens can refresh. The `ConfigWatcher` that tells them lives as long as the server. After a week of uptime the server spends seconds on every change, and a heap dump shows the watcher holding a listener for every session that was ever opened.

items: `open()`: from now on, every changed key reaches this session's `onChange(...)`;
`close()`: from now on, this session hears nothing, and the watcher holds nothing of it.

blocks.text: Other sessions on the same watcher are open at the same time, and closing one must not affect them. You may add a field. About four lines in total.

cases.says: an open session hears every changed key, in order
two open sessions on one watcher both hear a change
after close() the session hears no more changes and the watcher holds no listener for it
closing one session removes only its own listener; another open session keeps hearing changes

origin.section: A Lambda's Identity Is Not Promised: Keep the Instance You Need to Find Again

concepts: Two lambda expressions with the same text are different objects, so a listener must be removed with the instance that was added.
